lessons.name: Signal Support in Combined Arms Operations

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: What are the three military leadership attributes in the lesson?
options: Honor, patriotism, and duty
Leading, developing, and achieving
Authority, decision-making, and leadership
Character, presence, and intellect

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which attribute provides the moral and ethical basis for doing what is right?
options: Physical fitness
Intellect
Presence
Character

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which trio constitutes the Army Core Values in this lesson?
options: Character, presence, and intellect
Integrity, initiative, and judgment
Honor, patriotism, and duty
Empathy, confidence, and resilience

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which Army Core Value puts Army values ahead of personal comfort and self-interest?
options: Honor
Patriotism
Warrior ethos
Duty

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which Core Value includes allegiance to the Constitution?
options: Patriotism
Duty
Honor
Empathy

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which Core Value emphasizes professionalism, initiative, and excellence in fulfilling obligations?
options: Honor
Confidence
Duty
Patriotism

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which quality allows a leader to understand another person's experience from that person's point of view?
options: Sound judgment
Resilience
Confidence
Empathy

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: What does warrior ethos help sustain?
options: Technical knowledge across several areas
The will to win while doing what is right
An authoritative image during formation
The ability to read another person's emotions

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which attribute includes the professional image a leader projects?
options: Intellect
Presence
Character
Duty

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which aspect of presence includes wearing the appropriate uniform with pride?
options: Confidence
Resilience
Military and professional bearing
Health and physical fitness

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which aspect of presence supports mental and emotional performance under added physical stress?
options: Military and professional bearing
Health and physical fitness
Interpersonal tact
Domain knowledge

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which aspect of presence helps soldiers control doubt and reduces team anxiety?
options: Professional bearing
Physical fitness
Confidence
Resilience

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which quality involves recovering from setbacks, shock, and stress?
options: Mental agility
Warrior ethos
Resilience
Confidence

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which set contains only components of leader presence?
options: Bearing, empathy, confidence, and resilience
Fitness, tact, confidence, and resilience
Bearing, fitness, judgment, and resilience
Bearing, fitness, confidence, and resilience

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which attribute includes the mental resources that shape conceptual abilities?
options: Intellect
Character
Presence
Confidence

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which intellectual quality involves anticipating and adapting to changing situations?
options: Sound judgment
Mental agility
Innovation
Domain knowledge

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which intellectual quality enables a leader to assess a situation and draw feasible conclusions?
options: Sound judgment
Innovation
Interpersonal tact
Mental agility

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: What is innovation in the lesson's model?
options: Understanding another person's emotions
Introducing something new
Adapting quickly to existing alternatives
Weighing evidence to reach a feasible conclusion

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which component combines awareness of others' perceptions, recognition of diversity, and self-control?
options: Interpersonal tact
Confidence
Domain knowledge
Mental agility

leadershipattributes:easy:leadershipattr.prompt: Which intellectual component is built from facts, beliefs, and logical assumptions across relevant areas?
options: Interpersonal tact
Warrior ethos
Resilience
Domain knowledge

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A leader declines an unofficial privilege that would benefit them at the expense of unit standards. Which Core Value is most directly demonstrated?
options: Empathy
Duty
Patriotism
Honor

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: At an orientation, a leader explains why service entails loyalty to the Constitution. Which Core Value does this illustrate?
options: Warrior ethos
Patriotism
Honor
Duty

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A shift leader notices that assigned handover checks were left incomplete and finishes them before relief arrives. Which Core Value is most directly expressed?
options: Honor
Empathy
Duty
Patriotism

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A soldier becomes quiet after a reassignment. Which response best applies empathy?
options: Ask how the reassignment has affected the soldier and listen to their account
Restate the assignment criteria and end the conversation
Offer a public commendation for meeting the new schedule
Tell the soldier how most teammates reacted to similar moves

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A team falls short repeatedly during a drill and is tempted to skip a required check. Which response best shows warrior ethos?
options: Continue the drill and record the unchecked step as complete
Keep practicing and complete the check to standard
Shift the drill to a task the team already does well
Pause the drill until an evaluator can revise the standard

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A leader hears how a schedule change affects soldiers with caregiving duties before working out an equitable response. Which part of character enabled the leader to understand those effects?
options: Patriotism
Honor
Empathy
Warrior ethos

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: At a formal inspection, which action best demonstrates military and professional bearing?
options: Wear the prescribed uniform correctly and maintain a composed, professional manner
Privately ask how the inspection schedule affects a soldier's family
Add conditioning sessions before the next field exercise
Reorganize the stations when an inspector becomes unavailable

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A platoon has sufficient technical skill but struggles to maintain concentration after sustained exertion. What aspect of presence should its leader prioritize before the next field activity?
options: Domain knowledge
Interpersonal tact
Professional bearing
Health and physical fitness

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A routine exercise is interrupted and soldiers start to doubt whether they can complete it. Which immediate leader behavior best applies confidence?
options: Study the team's recovery rate after the event
Postpone the next exercise to build endurance
Check whether everyone is in the prescribed uniform
State the remaining achievable tasks calmly and show conviction that the team can execute them

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: After a failed evaluation, a leader regains composure, reviews the setback, and resumes purposeful work. Which aspect of presence is illustrated by the recovery?
options: Military bearing
Resilience
Physical fitness
Confidence

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A team has lost confidence after a setback. Which observation best shows the leader's own resilience?
options: The leader resumed effective work after the setback
The leader's initial briefing reassured an anxious audience
The leader inspected uniform and equipment standards
The leader predicted the team's strongest training event

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: Which corrective action directly develops the aspect of presence associated with professional image at ceremonies?
options: Review technical manuals on task equipment
Practice recovering and refocusing after interruptions
Rehearse appropriate uniform wear and carriage
Schedule a facilitated discussion on duty

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A leader understands the drill but communicates in a visibly hesitant manner that increases team doubt. Which component should the leader develop?
options: Confidence
Domain knowledge
Physical fitness
Resilience

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A room closes unexpectedly and the leader immediately rearranges the lesson across available spaces. Which intellect component does the quick adaptation most directly show?
options: Interpersonal tact
Mental agility
Domain knowledge
Sound judgment

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A leader compares travel time, staff availability, and training objectives before selecting a feasible schedule. Which intellect component is most directly applied?
options: Innovation
Interpersonal tact
Mental agility
Sound judgment

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: Which proposal most directly shows innovation in a unit's equipment handover process?
options: Move handover to the alternate room already in the plan
Check the manual to confirm the existing servicing intervals
Follow the approved handover checklist more consistently
Introduce a new handover method that captures recurring faults at the point of transfer

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: During a tense meeting, a leader recognizes that phrasing was received as a personal criticism and restates the point calmly. Which intellectual quality was most directly applied?
options: Technical domain knowledge
Sound judgment
Interpersonal tact
Innovation

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: Which preparation most directly builds domain knowledge for supervising a new training activity?
options: Rehearse switching quickly between two venues
Practice presenting decisions with a composed tone
Study the equipment, task procedures, and relevant training constraints
Write a reflection on recovery after failure

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A coordinator quickly substitutes an established indoor activity after lightning makes the field unavailable. What makes this mental agility?
options: The coordinator adapted quickly using an existing method
The coordinator created a novel form of instruction
The coordinator reduced concern through confident reassurance
The coordinator reviewed historical safety records

leadershipattributes:medium:leadershipat.prompt: A leader already understands a soldier's concern but must correct a misconception without humiliating the soldier in front of peers. Which skill now matters most?
options: Empathy for the soldier
Interpersonal tact
Domain knowledge
Resilience

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A report is due before close of business and a superior hints that a bad result should be removed for appearance. Which response meets duty and honor together?
options: Submit the edited report on time and preserve the raw result privately
Submit the accurate report on time through the proper channel
Delay the report until the result can be repeated and omitted
Ask a peer to sign the edited report while keeping the original

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader invokes love of country to justify abandoning assigned coordination work for a visible civic event. Which assessment best applies the lesson?
options: Patriotism is sufficient evidence of duty whenever the public event is worthwhile
Honor requires accepting the more visible assignment first
Duty applies only to mission execution, so coordination can be left to volunteers
Patriotism motivates service. Duty requires completing the assigned work.

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader understands a soldier's embarrassment but offers corrective feedback in front of peers with needlessly blunt wording. Which diagnosis best matches the evidence?
options: Both empathy and interpersonal tact are evident
The conduct primarily demonstrates domain knowledge and resilience
Empathy is evident, and interpersonal tact is weak
Interpersonal tact is evident, and empathy is weak

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: After repeated failures, a team can win an exercise by claiming an unearned result or keep trying to standard. Why does only the second course fit warrior ethos?
options: It prioritizes visible mission completion over the means used
It demands persistence while upholding the standard.
It relies on technical knowledge to redefine success after the fact
It protects the team's public image and avoids the discomfort of disclosure

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader empathizes with a friend who asks for a standards exception unavailable to others. Which action best preserves both empathy and honor?
options: Apply the standard and close the discussion before hearing the circumstances
Approve the exception quietly and avoid disclosing the reason
Listen to the concern and explore support that fits the same standards applied to everyone
Wait for someone else to deny the request and then offer support

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader has professional bearing and evaluates options well but knowingly rewards a friend outside the standards. Which conclusion best follows?
options: Evidence of presence and intellect does not establish sound character
Favoritism primarily shows weak mental agility under uncertainty
Professional bearing establishes sound character when the technical analysis is accurate
Professional appearance offsets the character concern if the unit meets its target

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader arrives unconditioned and loses concentration early, then recovers psychologically after a later failure. How should the two observations be classified?
options: Weak resilience and demonstrated confidence
Weak professional bearing and demonstrated fitness
Poor conditioning and demonstrated resilience
Weak confidence and demonstrated mental agility

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader arrives in perfect uniform but increases soldiers' anxiety by wavering over an achievable task. Which diagnosis points to the missing element?
options: The leader shows physical fitness and needs stronger bearing
The leader shows confidence and needs stronger bearing
The leader shows resilience and needs greater physical fitness
Strong bearing and insufficient confidence

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader sounds certain during a disruption but chooses a schedule that requires more people than are available. Which evaluation is best supported?
options: Confidence is evident, and sound judgment is lacking
The schedule demonstrates both physical fitness and mental agility
Sound judgment is evident, and confidence is lacking
The schedule demonstrates both confidence and sound judgment

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: During a long exercise, an anxious team gets a steady briefing but still shows declining concentration under exertion. Which follow-up addresses the remaining gap?
options: Shift the focus to uniform and carriage before every drill
Replace conditioning with a more authoritative briefing style
Improve conditioning before future exercises while retaining clear, confident briefings
Evaluate recovery after setbacks and leave conditioning unchanged

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: Which pair of observations separately supports confidence and resilience, in that order?
options: Reassuring the team, then recovering after a setback
Maintaining a professional appearance, then increasing physical endurance
Regaining performance after a setback, then reassuring the team during uncertainty
Choosing a feasible plan, then replacing it when conditions change

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A physically prepared leader projects authority during inspection but remains unable to resume effective work after a major setback. Which targeted development best fits the evidence?
options: Increase endurance training as the sole corrective action
Teach additional facts about the inspection process
Repeat uniform and appearance inspections more often
Practice structured recovery and re-engagement after realistic setbacks

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: After a failed drill, a leader both returns to effective work and refuses to compromise standards to claim success. Which classification is strongest?
options: Returning to effective work shows resilience. Persisting to standard shows warrior ethos.
Returning to effective work shows bearing. Persisting to standard shows physical fitness.
Returning to effective work shows tact. Persisting to standard shows domain knowledge.
Returning to effective work shows confidence. Persisting to standard shows mental agility.

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader reacts quickly to a closure by selecting a pre-approved alternative. A teammate later designs a reusable method that the unit adopts. How do the two actions differ?
options: Both primarily demonstrate interpersonal tact
Both primarily demonstrate innovation
The first shows innovation and the second shows mental agility
The first shows mental agility and the second shows innovation

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader accurately recalls equipment limits yet chooses a plan requiring performance beyond them. What is the best interpretation?
options: The leader knows the limits but misjudges feasibility
Sound judgment is evident, but domain knowledge is absent
Interpersonal tact is demonstrated because the plan balances differing views
Mental agility is demonstrated because the proposed plan is ambitious

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A new scheduling method would reduce idle time but cannot meet a fixed qualification requirement. Which action best combines innovation with sound judgment?
options: Report the projected efficiency gain and leave the qualification issue to individual teams
Pilot a compliant version and compare results before expanding.
Return to the old method and treat all future experiments as unacceptable
Adopt the new method because any reduction in idle time demonstrates feasibility

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: Two leaders correctly identify what upset a soldier. Which added observation specifically supports a claim of interpersonal tact?
options: One can recall a wider range of administrative procedures
One adjusts the timing and wording of feedback after recognizing how it will be received
One can describe the soldier's likely emotions in greater detail
One has recovered from a similar setback in the past

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A leader responds to a sudden constraint by generating several alternatives but picks one without checking a known time limit. Which diagnosis is best?
options: Both mental agility and sound judgment are demonstrated by the final selection
Domain knowledge is necessarily missing because the decision was infeasible
Mental agility is evident and sound judgment needs improvement
Sound judgment is evident and mental agility needs improvement

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: The team can solve a planning problem but keeps reaching technically infeasible decisions because assumptions are treated as verified facts. Which change targets the intellectual failure most directly?
options: Increase confidence by briefing the chosen option more forcefully
Separate facts from assumptions and test proposed choices against confirmed limits
Require a novel alternative before anyone discusses constraints
Reduce disagreement by letting the most senior planner decide first

leadershipattributes:hard:leadershipattr.prompt: A technically expert leader avoids tense discussions by issuing correct instructions in a way that repeatedly alienates subordinates. What would improve the relevant gap while keeping the technical standard?
options: Demonstrate resilience by ignoring feedback after each exchange
Replace the requirement with whatever attracts the least resistance
Add more technical detail and leave the manner of delivery unchanged
Keep the requirement and adapt the manner of delivery to the audience's perceptions

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What does leadership provide in order to influence people?
options: Authority, resources, and reports
Knowledge, confidence, and resilience
Schedules, standards, and rewards
Purpose, direction, and motivation

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What two outcomes does the lesson's leadership definition emphasize?
options: Exercise authority and manage the budget
Meet the schedule and complete documentation
Accomplish the mission and improve the organization
Maintain individual proficiency and set training standards

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What is a core leader competency?
options: A formal position in a chain of command
A personal value acquired through experience
A technical certificate held by a commander
An essential ability of a person who leads

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which factors does the lesson name when discussing dimensions of the operational environment?
options: Weather, terrain, and the day-night cycle
Rank structure, tenure, and specialty
Motivation, incentives, and public recognition
Time in service, education, and technical aptitude

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What completes the transition from possessing relevant attributes to effective leadership action?
options: Acquiring more professional knowledge alone
Applying core leader competencies
Memorizing the definition of leadership
Obtaining appointment authority

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What are the three competency categories used in this lesson?
options: Purpose, direction, and motivation
Character, presence, and intellect
Planning, preparing, and executing
Leading, developing, and achieving

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Under which leading subset does enforcing standards appear?
options: Leads others
Extends influence beyond the chain of command
Leads by example
Communicates

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which leading subset includes understanding the limits of one's influence outside formal authority?
options: Communicates
Leads by example
Extends influence beyond the chain of command
Leads others

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which behavior belongs to leads by example?
options: Demonstrating competence in one's own conduct
Setting and enforcing standards for subordinates
Ensuring the listeners share an understanding
Negotiating consensus outside the chain of command

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which activity belongs to the communicates subset?
options: Demonstrating competence through personal example
Negotiating consensus with an outside partner
Balancing mission and soldier welfare
Listening actively

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What balance does the lesson include under leads others?
options: Short-term objectives and a long-term vision
Mission needs and soldier welfare
Planning effort and monitoring effort
Professional knowledge and conceptual ability

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What is a central aim of developing competency?
options: Maintain the existing standard until turnover
Focus the organization on only the current task
Leave the organization better than one found it
Use formal authority to settle every disagreement

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which set names all three developing subsets in the deck?
options: Prepare self, enforce standards, communicate
Create a positive environment, monitor performance, negotiate consensus
Create a positive environment, prepare self, develop others
Develop others, lead by example, accomplish missions

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which developing subset concerns the leader's own readiness?
options: Create a positive environment
Develop others
Prepare self
Develop and execute a plan

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What time horizon should a developing leader consider?
options: Only the deadlines on the current mission
Both short-term and long-term goals
Only the current reporting period
Only goals that extend beyond the current command

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What does achieving begin with in the short term?
options: Preparing a succession plan
Negotiating across organizational boundaries
Reinforcing completed performance
Setting objectives

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: What guides achieving in the long term?
options: A list of recently completed tasks
A clear vision
A uniform performance schedule
A briefing on formal authority

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which action is an achieving subset in the deck?
options: Extending influence beyond the chain of command
Providing direction, guidance, and priorities
Demonstrating personal competence
Creating a positive environment

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which activity is listed under accomplishing missions?
options: Monitoring performance
Listening actively
Preparing self
Stating goals for action

leadershipcompetencies:easy:leadershipco.prompt: Which sequence belongs under developing and executing a plan?
options: Planning, preparing, and executing
Setting standards, building trust, and resolving conflict
Prioritizing, mentoring, and recognizing
Listening, negotiating, and coaching

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: Which opening best applies the lesson's definition when introducing a joint training task to subordinates?
options: Explain why the task matters, what to do, and how it helps the team
Remind teams who is in charge and announce when the roster will be finalized
Describe why the task matters and leave all responsibilities to later discussion
Distribute the task list and allow each team to infer its purpose

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A daytime rehearsal was successful but the same activity will run in darkness after rain. Which adjustment best applies the lesson's environmental guidance?
options: Reassess visibility, weather effects, and terrain before confirming the rehearsal plan
Rotate leaders to create additional development opportunities
Reuse the timing estimates and add a longer post-event review
Retain daytime timings and focus the brief on individual motivation

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A new leader can explain the standards and describe the model but has yet to apply either while directing a team. What assessment activity best checks the remaining gap?
options: Ask the leader to summarize another team's results
Review the leader's course certificates and written notes
Observe the leader applying competencies in a team exercise
Ask the leader to recite the attributes and competency names

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A peer unit controls a shared facility and reports through a different chain. What approach best applies the relevant leading subset?
options: Deliver a demonstration without addressing how the facility will be shared
Direct its team to change its schedule on the strength of your own unit's priorities
Build trust with its leader and negotiate access that respects both units' authority
Set a new internal roster and assume the peer unit will follow it

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A leader sees inconsistent compliance with a clearly established standard across their subordinate teams. Which action best fits leads others?
options: Ask an outside organization to create a replacement standard
Have teams report results without discussing the standard
Concentrate on demonstrating the task without addressing recurring violations
Restate the standard and correct deviations consistently

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A leader says accurate handovers matter. What added action best demonstrates leading by example?
options: Ask an outside section to adopt the same reporting format
Issue the handover schedule to the team again
Quiz soldiers on the purpose of handovers
Follow the required process in their own handover

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: After a briefing, two teams describe different responsibilities for the same task. Which action best applies communicates?
options: Assign the disputed work to a third team without discussing roles
Listen to each team's interpretation, clarify responsibilities, and check their revised understanding
Send the same briefing unchanged and record both teams as informed
Evaluate each team against the original briefing after the event

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A task must be completed today, and one team has already worked a long shift. Which choice best balances the mission with welfare?
options: Shift essential work to rested staff and defer lower priorities
Assign the most demanding portion to the fatigued team and reduce its paperwork
Cancel every task until the same team is rested
Continue the whole task list with the fatigued team because it knows the work

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: Two support teams disagree about shared training time. Which action most directly uses the conflict-resolution element of extended influence?
options: Surface both needs and broker a workable schedule
Publish one team's preference as an informal recommendation
Demonstrate how your own team uses the facility
Evaluate each team separately on compliance with its own schedule

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A leader will soon oversee an unfamiliar process. Which step best applies prepare self?
options: Assign a junior leader to study the process independently
Write a list of short-term outputs for the section
Assess their own gaps and practice the skills needed for the new responsibility
Add another company-wide feedback session

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A junior leader can execute a task but needs practice supervising it. Which choice best applies develop others?
options: Require more individual repetitions of the task at the same skill level
Have the junior leader observe while a senior leader remains responsible for every decision
Direct the junior leader to write a schedule without assigning a team
Give the junior leader a supervised opportunity to lead and provide feedback afterward

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: Personnel conceal minor mistakes because discussions routinely become personal. Which intervention best supports creating a positive environment?
options: Discuss mistakes only when the reporting period ends
Ask one experienced leader to handle every correction
Require the reporting team to wait for a peer unit to raise concerns first
Set respectful review norms and recognize accurate reporting of mistakes

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: How should a leader apply developing competency when an urgent milestone coincides with a longer-term proficiency goal?
options: Ask a peer organization to choose which goal the unit should drop
Meet the immediate requirement and deliberately protect a realistic opportunity to build proficiency
Suspend the proficiency goal indefinitely after the milestone is assigned
Dedicate every work period to long-term practice until proficiency is reached

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A leader wants the unit to stay capable after a turnover. Which action most directly addresses developing others?
options: Keep every critical decision at the current leader's level
Increase the cadence of formal performance reports
Coach several successors in key duties
Write a schedule for the leader's personal professional reading

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: Two teams are busy but working toward different outcomes. Which first action best applies achieving through direction and priorities?
options: Begin preparing a future succession plan
Name the common result, establish which tasks take precedence, and assign responsibility
Ask the teams to nominate peers for training
Keep both workstreams and compare effort once the deadline passes

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A company has an approved plan but has not rehearsed unfamiliar assignments or assembled resources. Which achieving activity is missing?
options: Preparing
Planning
Monitoring performance
Reinforcing good performance

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A leader wants to know during an activity whether execution is on track. Which action applies monitoring performance?
options: Wait until the final result to restate the original objectives
Check milestones against the plan and flag deviations early
Develop the next operation's objectives before checking the current work
Recognize every team regardless of observed performance

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A team consistently delivers accurate handovers under time pressure. What action best reinforces that good performance?
options: Record the outcome and require a new method for the next handover
Wait for a decline before mentioning the behavior
Recognize the specific effective behavior and incorporate it into subsequent handovers
Shift recognition to the team with the greatest headcount

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: A work section meets a deadline by drawing on its last qualified operator every night. What next action best supports achieving over time?
options: Extend the same arrangement until each later deadline is reached
Lower the stated objective to the effort that was already expended
Track attendance more closely without changing coverage
Maintain output while restoring qualified backup coverage

leadershipcompetencies:medium:leadership.prompt: Which response fits improving organizational performance after several handover errors recur?
options: Set a deadline for the next handover without examining the errors
Use error records to revise the process, then track repeat errors
Add a second schedule for reporting hours worked
Praise the unit for completing the handovers on time

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: A manager obtains timely compliance by threatening penalties, but soldiers do not understand the task's purpose and the same defects recur. What conclusion is best supported?
options: Formal direction produced compliance, but the broader leadership outcome remains unmet
Timely compliance establishes that purpose, motivation, and organizational improvement were achieved
The deficiency can be diagnosed solely as weak professional appearance
The recurring defects indicate only a failure to possess domain knowledge

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: Two teams have equal technical knowledge. One recognizes that nighttime terrain has changed the movement timeline and adapts how it coordinates the work. What distinguishes its leadership performance?
options: It applied competencies to relevant operational conditions
It demonstrated a longer time horizon by keeping the original timeline
It increased technical knowledge merely by changing its coordination approach
It substituted terrain familiarity for every other leadership requirement

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: Which evidence most strongly supports all three categories at a company event?
options: The leader settled a disagreement, established consensus, and retained every leadership role
The leader aligned teams on purpose, coached junior leads, and delivered the intended outcome
The leader published a schedule, distributed a roster, and restated the schedule
The leader practiced an unfamiliar skill, recorded the results, and scheduled more self-study

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: A neighboring unit agrees to lend resources, but the terms exceed what its representative can authorize. What best preserves effective external influence?
options: Treat the representative's verbal agreement as sufficient to avoid further delay
Confirm each side's authority and negotiate within the limits or involve the appropriate decision-makers
Cancel coordination and send both teams the same message about responsibilities
Ask your subordinates to enforce the arrangement with the neighboring unit

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: A commander communicates a standard clearly, checks understanding, and exempts themselves from meeting it. Which distinction explains the loss of credibility?
options: Both behaviors primarily demonstrate enforcing standards
Leading by example was demonstrated, and communicates was undermined
Both behaviors primarily demonstrate extended influence
Communicates was demonstrated, and leading by example was undermined

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: A staff lead listens to both teams and accurately summarizes their views. The teams still interpret their handoff responsibilities differently. Which step closes the remaining communication gap?
options: Reduce the number of handoff points without discussing their ownership
Negotiate a new relationship with an unrelated partner
Agree on the handoff and have both teams repeat their roles
Model the uniform and conduct expected at the handoff

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: A leader can complete a task fastest by keeping an exhausted crew working. A trained relief crew is available if the plan is adjusted. Which decision aligns with leading and achieving?
options: Retain the tired crew and treat rapid completion as sufficient evidence of success
Rotate the crews without restating priorities or checking progress
Pause the full operation until the original crew can finish
Assign essential work to the rested crew and check progress

leadershipcompetencies:hard:leadershipco.prompt: A commander coaches subordinates well but repeatedly fails to secure cooperation from a separate organization. The counterpart cites conflicting priorities. What competency should the commander apply directly?
options: Prepare self by reviewing personal training goals for the year
Extend influence by learning the counterpart's constraints and negotiating a shared solution
Develop others by giving subordinates more practice with current duties
Lead by example by personally meeting the company's internal task standard

An enemy reserve battalion waits behind a mountain ridge that keeps its primary weapons from firing on friendly units, but it could move to counterattack within hours. The brigade commander wants the reserve's movement held back long enough for the attack to reach its objective. Which role-and-effect pairing best fits the commander's aim?
options: Close support to destroy the reserve now, because the reserve is already firing on the brigade's lead units.
Counterfires to neutralize the reserve, because reserves form part of the total enemy fire-support system.
Attack at depth to disrupt and delay the reserve, opening a window for the brigade's maneuver.
Attack at depth to divert the reserve, drawing its attention away from the brigade's principal attack.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-04.prompt: Enemy guns have been shelling a Philippine Army battalion across a wide sector. Sound-and-flash reports and drone imagery now also locate enemy forward observers and an enemy fire-direction post. The division commander wants enemy fires reduced across the whole sector, not only from the gun that fired most recently. Which targeting approach best matches both the tactical role and the commander's intent?
options: Close support against the single gun that fired last, since it is the element directly threatening the battalion.
Attack at depth against the observers and fire-direction post, since neither can fire a primary weapon at friendly troops.
Hold fires until drone imagery confirms each gun, since sound-and-flash reports are not artillery information collectors.
Counterfires against the located guns, observers, and fire-direction post as parts of the enemy fire-support system.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-05.prompt: A Philippine Army brigade is defending a coastal town, and its supporting battery is positioned to the rear as planned. Enemy troops penetrate the forward line and fire on a company, which immediately requests artillery. The battery is midway through a planned mission against enemy forces massing far to the north, and its guns can reach both targets from where they stand. Which response best applies the lesson?
options: Shift fires promptly to close support of the company from the current position, since shifting does not require displacement.
Complete the northern mission first, since a planned mission takes precedence over an unplanned request.
Displace the battery forward toward the company before firing, since supporting fires must come from well-forward positions.
Treat the penetration as counterfire work, since enemy troops inside the line form part of the enemy fire-support system.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-06.prompt: A typhoon grounds a Philippine Army task force's drones and aircraft for two days while its infantry remains in contact in rugged terrain. The artillery battalion's MET section can still provide current data, and ground observers remain with the forward companies. A staff officer recommends suspending artillery support until drone imagery returns. Which recommendation best fits the lesson?
options: Suspend fires until the weather clears, because drone imagery is the lesson's required source of target information.
Continue fires through the storm, using ground observers to locate targets and current MET data for accuracy.
Continue fires, but move the guns before engaging each new target, since weather prevents shifting fires.
Continue fires, but limit them to suppression, since storm conditions make MET data unusable for predicted fires.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-07.prompt: A single enemy bunker blocks a Philippine Army platoon that must clear a trail junction within 30 minutes. Ammunition resupply across the strait is delayed by rough seas, and the battery's stocks must last until the next landing. The platoon leader needs the bunker's fire kept down only while the platoon moves past. Which fire plan best balances the lesson's capabilities and limitations?
options: Fire a destruction mission until the bunker is permanently out of action, since destruction gives the platoon the most lasting protection.
Decline the mission until resupply arrives, since artillery cannot engage a point target economically.
Suppress the bunker with a suitable shell-and-fuze combination for the movement window, conserving ammunition.
Mass the whole battalion on the bunker, since rapid massing removes the ammunition cost of destroying point targets.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-08.prompt: A Philippine Army battery has fired many missions from one position, and enemy drones have been seen overhead. The supported battalion will need fires again within the hour, and the battery has no dedicated security or air-defense element nearby. Which course of action best weighs the battery's exposure against the battalion's need for support?
options: Remain in place, since artillery can shift and mass its fires without displacing and so has no reason to move.
Cease firing until the drones depart, since a silent position presents no firing signature to detect.
Stay and defend the position, since artillery fires under all conditions and can protect itself from attack.
Displace judiciously to an alternate position, timing the move so fires are ready when the battalion needs them.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-09.prompt: For a Philippine Army inter-island move, the first vessel can carry only medium-caliber weapons that are classified as towed. The movement list gives five weapons with their caliber and transport classification: 120 mm towed, 121 mm towed, 160 mm self-propelled, 210 mm towed, and 121 mm aerial. Which weapon or weapons belong on the first vessel?
options: The 121 mm towed weapon only
The 121 mm towed and 121 mm aerial weapons
The 121 mm towed and 210 mm towed weapons
The 121 mm towed and 160 mm self-propelled weapons

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-10.prompt: A Philippine Army battalion communications plan assumes that every firing unit uses the same radio. One battery has 105 mm towed weapons and the other has 155 mm self-propelled weapons. Before issuing radios for an island operation, the signal officer must record each battery's caliber class, transport class, and issued radio as the lesson describes. Which record is correct?
options: 105 mm: light, towed, Harris; 155 mm: medium, self-propelled, Harris
105 mm: light, towed, Harris; 155 mm: medium, self-propelled, manet
105 mm: light, towed, Harris; 155 mm: heavy, self-propelled, manet
105 mm: medium, towed, Harris; 155 mm: medium, self-propelled, manet

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-11.prompt: A Philippine Army company will cross a river under observation from an enemy weapons position on the far ridge. The crossing takes only a short time, and ammunition must be conserved for the next phase. The commander needs the position unable to interfere with the crossing while it lasts, but does not need it out of action for a long period. Which planned effect and computed minimum best match this requirement?
options: Destroy, planning for at least 30 percent so the position cannot recover before the crossing
Suppress, planning for at least 10 percent because suppression also lasts only a short time
Neutralize, planning for at least 10-percent computed casualties or materiel damage
Neutralize, planning for at least 3 percent because the effect is needed for a brief crossing

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-12.prompt: A Philippine Army task force has a short fire-support window before its principal landing on fictional Isla Maragat. Enemy reserves remain able to fight, but a river line and obstacles on the coast road offer a chance to break their timetable. A feint on a neighboring island could draw enemy attention and forces away. The desired end state is that the island's defenders lose the physical means or will to fight; there is no evidence of 30-percent damage. Which fire plan should the cell recommend for this window?
options: Use route fires for diversion, the island feint for disruption, and loss of means or will to judge defeat.
Use fires with terrain to disrupt reserve timing, the feint to divert forces, and cessation of resistance to judge destruction.
Use fires with obstacles to disrupt reserve timing, the feint to divert forces, and withdrawal from the road to establish defeat.
Use fires with terrain and obstacles to disrupt reserve timing, the feint to divert forces from the landing, and loss of means or will to judge defeat.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-13.prompt: Philippine Army target acquisition locates a single enemy radar vehicle that has been detecting friendly batteries by their firing signatures. The division wants it out of action for a long period so it cannot support the enemy's next phase, but the battalion's ammunition for the week is limited. Which planning statement best reflects the lesson?
options: Plan destruction at 30 percent and budget considerable ammunition, since the radar is a point target.
Plan neutralization at 10 percent, since a short interruption will keep the radar from locating the batteries.
Plan suppression at 3 percent, since some degradation of the radar will protect the batteries for the week.
Plan destruction at 30 percent with a small allocation, since massing fires removes the point-target cost.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-14.prompt: After a Philippine Army battalion's artillery preparation, the computed estimate for an enemy company shows 12-percent casualties and materiel damage. Observers report that the company withdrew from the objective with most weapons still serviceable. Intercepted orders then direct its surviving crews to resume resistance, but the crews refuse and say they will no longer fight. The brigade asks how to report the effect. Which label is best supported?
options: Destruction, because giving up the objective shows the company is out of action for a long period
Defeat, because the company has lost the will to fight
Diversion, because the company's attention and forces were drawn away from the objective
Suppression, because a 12-percent estimate indicates a temporary drop in performance

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-15.prompt: A Philippine Army artillery battalion must move from Tambuli Island to neighboring Isla Maragat, where a brigade lands tomorrow, while the brigade still on Tambuli remains in contact for two more days. The battalion's KM450, KM250, and M35 vehicles and a landing craft are available. Which movement plan best satisfies the lesson's archipelagic requirement?
options: Move the entire battalion tonight in one lift, since the lesson's requirement is speed of displacement between islands.
Keep the entire battalion on Tambuli until contact there ends, since displacement must not disrupt ongoing operations.
Move in echelons, keeping part of the battalion firing on Tambuli while an element with fire direction and radios crosses.
Send the guns across first and bring fire direction and radios only after the fighting on Tambuli ends.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-16.prompt: After a rapid Philippine Army displacement, one battery fires from Isla Maragat while two batteries remain on Tambuli Island. Each island's batteries were located using a different local reference, and current MET data are already available to all three. The battalion now wants to mass all three batteries on a landing-beach target between the islands. Which step should come first?
options: Mass immediately, since artillery can shift and mass fires rapidly without a requirement to displace.
Rely on the current MET data, since meteorology is the requirement that makes massed predicted fires accurate.
Move the Tambuli batteries to Isla Maragat, since massing fires requires the batteries to share one island.
Have the survey section place all three batteries on one common grid of location and direction.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-17.prompt: A Philippine Army brigade's concept of operations reserves most of the battery's ammunition for fires at H-hour on the main objective. Two hours earlier, a flank company in contact requests fires against a small enemy team firing on it. Answering with a full preparation would consume the H-hour allocation. Which response best satisfies the basic tasks?
options: Answer the company promptly with a limited mission and keep the H-hour allocation for the main objective.
Fire the full preparation for the company, since support to forces in contact outranks the concept of operations.
Refuse the request, since the concept of operations commits the battery's ammunition to the main objective.
Delay the company's mission until after H-hour, then use whatever ammunition remains to support it.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-18.prompt: In a Philippine Army brigade attack up the fictional Kalumpang valley, the draft fire plan assigns artillery, mortars, and attack helicopters to the same trench line at the same time, while an enemy machine-gun post on the flanking spur has no fire assigned. A washed-out road limits artillery resupply. Which revision best applies the lesson's basic tasks?
options: Keep every asset on the trench line, since massing all fires on one target produces the greatest effect.
Synchronize the plan by distributing the available fire-support assets across both targets to economize and maximize effect.
Remove the mortars and helicopters so the artillery alone engages both targets without coordinating other assets.
Keep the plan but raise the artillery's ammunition allocation, since sustainment corrects duplicated fires.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-19.prompt: A Philippine Army battery commander deployed on a small island stops sending ammunition and fuel status reports, reasoning that battalion logistics will notice any shortage. After three days of firing, the battery runs low just as the supported battalion begins its main effort. Which assessment best reflects the lesson?
options: Battalion logistics alone failed, since sustaining artillery is a higher-headquarters function that batteries do not share.
The mobility element failed, since vehicles such as the KM450 and M35 exist to carry resupply to firing units.
The battery commander shares the sustainment task, since commanders at all levels must sustain artillery units.
No task failed, since artillery can fire under all conditions and its capability does not depend on supply.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-20.prompt: In a large Philippine Army multi-brigade operation, an observer's sound-and-flash location and drone imagery point to different enemy firing positions. Brigade wants fire commands quickly, but an inaccurate location would waste the short fire-support window. Which response resolves the conflicting target information while keeping artillery-intelligence work and call-for-fire conversion with the appropriate elements?
options: Have the fire direction center reconcile the locations, then make the Target Acquisition Platoon convert the observer's call while the intelligence office only relays reports.
Have the Signal Platoon determine the target location, the intelligence office convert the call, and the fire direction center relay the resulting commands.
Send the first drone image straight to the fire direction center for commands and resolve the conflicting location later through the acquisition platoon and intelligence office.

Use the Target Acquisition Platoon to collect, process, and disseminate accurately located target information; the FA Regiment and FA Bn Intelligence Office remains the principal artillery-intelligence unit in this large operation, then the fire direction center converts the observer's call into commands.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-21.prompt: A Philippine Army observer calls for fire on an enemy platoon spread across an area wider than one gun can adequately cover. The nearest single gun could fire first; the full battery is farther away but within range; a second battery is beyond its specified range. Which fire-direction decision best reflects the lesson?
options: Convert the call into commands for the full battery, a group of weapons suited to cover the target.
Assign the nearest single gun, since the quickest response is what fire coordination seeks.
Convert the call into commands for both batteries, since massing overrides the second battery's range limit.
Return the call to the observer, since converting a call into fire commands is the observer's responsibility.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-22.prompt: A Philippine Army battalion plans predicted night fires against targets that no observer can see. Its MET section in Headquarters and Headquarters Battery has current data, but the voice and digital radio link between the MET section and the fire direction center keeps failing. Which action best protects the accuracy of the planned fires?
options: Proceed on the survey grid alone, since survey and MET both belong to the same headquarters battery.
Restore reliable communication so the current MET data reach the fire direction center before firing.
Proceed without MET data, since artillery can provide fires under all conditions of weather.
Have the Target Acquisition Platoon estimate MET data, since it is the eyes and ears of the system.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-23.prompt: A Philippine Army infantry company will hold a small outlying island for a week, and the brigade wants the smallest artillery commitment the lesson supports. options: Send one gun section attached informally, since a single weapon is the easiest load for a landing craft.
Send an FA platoon with no set relationship, since being nearby is enough to coordinate its fires.
Send an FA platoon with an established command or support relationship to the company.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-24.prompt: A Philippine Army brigade has seized its objective with its supporting artillery battalion positioned well forward. options: Stay well forward, since the battalion must keep exploiting its weapons' range against the counterattack.
Push farther forward to meet the counterattack at depth before it reaches the brigade's new line.
Hold the current positions, since the battalion can shift and mass fires without repositioning.
Reposition toward the rear, so the battalion's fires can continue if the enemy penetrates the line.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-25.prompt: A Philippine Army brigade launches an attack deep across a fictional province. Which decision best integrates the lesson?
options: Position well forward to support the attack and exploit range, displacing judiciously to limit exposure.
Stay in the rear, since rearward positions are what protect the continuity of fires.
Stay in the rear and mass fires on nearer targets, since massing makes up for the lost range.

Destruction keeps a target out of action permanently or for a long time; neutralization, for a short time.

fieldartillery:hard:fieldartillery-h-28.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes 'Defeat' from 'Destroy' as tactical mission tasks?
options: Defeat: enemy is combat-ineffective until reconstituted; destroy: enemy has lost the means or will to fight.

Eyes and ears: survey; brain: fire direction; muscle: logistics and mobility

Treat the repeated claim as disproved because copying always changes source accuracy
